title: A cause that explains the difference
statement: In a comparison item, the keyed explanation must name a cause that differs between the things compared; a cause that applies to both explains nothing about the difference.
detail: One of eight copy-task audits added to an item evaluator for issue 962 fails a keyed explanation that applies equally to both subjects of a comparison, since it explains the general direction of change rather than the difference (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`). The audit fires only on data tables comparing exactly two named subjects (the same file, line 102), and it rests on one rubric, not a measurement.

evidence.quote: If the correct answer's causal explanation applies equally to both subjects, it explains the general direction of change for all subjects — not the specific comparative difference.
